conviction_note: Two measurements that roughly agree: the findings sum to -2.0. A likely beat of the Q3 guide, which this name has beaten on both 2026 prints, is outweighed by Q4-guide risk: Academic is falling about 23% q/q, Skilling has decelerated against a company 'double-digit FY growth' claim, and Coursera's consumer business softened on Oct 29. The scaled number is (2*0.47-1)*15 = -0.9. p_up sits at 47, near 50, because the bear case rests on proxies and inference while net cash is about half the market cap and a 9.4-day short gives the upside its own mechanism. Last quarter shows the reaction can override the print: a beat of about 4.6% on revenue and roughly 65% on EBITDA was sold 14.6% on the guide.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue $43.5M: company guide $43-44M (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm, 2026-08-06), with consensus $43.5M on Benzinga (https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CHGG/earnings-forecasts) and $43.52M on Yahoo from one analyst (https://finance.yahoo.com/quote/CHGG/analysis/). The bar is the guide midpoint, so it is sourced (company guide plus two agreeing estimate sources) but rests on about one analyst. No Q4 consensus was found, and the Q4 guide is the line the stock has traded on.

findings.finding: Chegg beat its own guide by a wide margin on both 2026 prints. Q2: revenue $51.8M against a $49-50M guide (+4.6% vs midpoint), adj. EBITDA $9.1M against $5-6M. Q1: revenue $63.3M, EPS $0.03 against -$0.02 consensus. Q3 consensus ($43.5M) sits exactly at the guide midpoint, so a repeat would print around $44.5-45.5M, about 2-4% over the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-08-06): a beat on revenue, EBITDA and cash was sold -14.56% on a Q3 guide 9.9% below estimates. Q1 2026 (2026-05-06): beat, +10.34% close-to-close per baseline, although one report put the intraday move at -13% on the Q2 outlook. The reaction follows the guide, not the beat.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus sits at the midpoint of the guide rather than at the company's habitual beat, so the estimate set has not priced the pattern. With one analyst, nobody is paid to model it. The cost: the beat is inside the range the company itself conditioned, and the stock has not rewarded beats.
findings.independence: The Q1 guide-vs-actual comes from a different document, the Q1 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001364954/000136495426000045/a9901-financialresultsq120.htm, Q2 guide $49-50M / adj. EBITDA $5-6M). Same company, same management habit.

findings.finding: Skilling is decelerating against the company's own full-year claim. In May the company said it expected 'double-digit Skilling revenue growth for the full year' with acceleration as the year went on. Instead Skilling grew +9% y/y in Q1 ($17.6M) and +2% in Q2 ($17.5M), and the Q2 release dropped the separate Skilling guide in favour of total revenue only. Full-year double-digit growth now needs high-teens growth in H2, so a walk-back or a miss on the growth narrative is likely at this print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guidance is what moved this name on its last prints: -14.56% (Aug 2026, Q3 guide cut), -10.67% (Feb 2026), -31.41% (Feb 2025). No print in the baseline shows a separate reaction to Skilling.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q2 deceleration is public, but the double-digit full-year claim was never formally withdrawn. Dropping the segment guide hid it rather than retracting it. If it were priced, the Q2 call coverage would have flagged the walk-back, and the summaries found do not.
findings.independence: Q2 Skilling +2% is from a separate document, the Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm). Net of the rest of the company: Skilling is about a third of revenue and Academic is falling far faster, so Skilling cannot carry the total either way. This finding is about the one growth story losing credibility, and is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: The Q3 guide implies Academic Services of about $26M ($43.5M total less about $17.5M Skilling), against $45.7M in Q1 and $34.3M in Q2: roughly -23% q/q and -60% y/y. Gross margin is guided to 48-49% from 57% non-GAAP, and adj. EBITDA to $1-2M from $9.1M. If that slope carries into Q4, the guide given at this print points to roughly breakeven or negative EBITDA and a revenue run-rate below $40M.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Q3 guide cut in Aug 2026 (revenue guide 9.9% below estimates) drove -14.56% despite a beat. The Q4 2024 guide in Feb 2025 drove -31.41%.
findings.why_not_priced: The Q3 guide is priced. The Q4 slope is not: no Q4 consensus was found, and with one analyst the extrapolation is not on any terminal. The case against: the company says it expects H2 free cash flow to stay positive, and Q3 is seasonally weak, so Q4 could stabilise. That uncertainty keeps this finding small.
findings.independence: Coursera's Q3 (separate finding) points the same way for consumer edtech. The deferred-revenue fall of 10% to $26.6M in the Q2 10-Q, as summarised by panabee (https://www.panabee.com/news/chegg-earnings-q2-2026-report, an AI summary), also points the same way. Shares the Q2 8-K with the beat finding, but reads a different line.

findings.finding: Peer read-through, reported after Chegg last spoke: Coursera's Q3 2026 (Oct 29) showed Consumer revenue down 9% y/y normalised, with one-time and transactional purchases falling and leading funnel indicators softening. On the call, management guided to further consumer deceleration in Q4 and a low-double-digit consumer decline in 2027.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No earlier Chegg reaction to a peer print is in the baseline. Chegg's own guide reactions are listed above.
findings.why_not_priced: The release came after Chegg's last guide (Aug 6), and CHGG has drifted only -1.8% over 20 days, so there was no visible repricing on the peer read. That said, it is a proxy: Coursera's consumer mix (degrees, certificates, Udemy) differs from Chegg Study and Busuu.
findings.independence: Call summary: https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/transcript-coursera-q3-earnings-call-highlights-2026-10-29/ (same event, so not independent). This is macro-to-company transmission that Chegg has not confirmed, so it is sized small.

findings.finding: Chegg has been debt-free since Sept 1, 2026, after repaying the remaining $33.9M of 0% converts at maturity. That leaves about $38M of pro forma cash against a market cap of about $78M, plus $120.7M of buyback authorisation and a stated expectation of positive free cash flow in H2. Cash is about half the market cap, which limits downside from a weak guide and leaves room for a buyback headline.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no precedent for a print carrying a buyback or a balance-sheet headline. The Q2 print had a $1.7M buyback and still fell 14.6%.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: the repayment was announced on Sept 1. What is not priced is how the Q3 cash balance compares with the roughly $38M pro forma figure: near-breakeven EBITDA plus severance tapering could show cash holding or rising, which would make net cash a larger share of market cap. Financing question answered: this was a repayment from cash, not a raise. No dilution and no going-concern language was found.
findings.independence: The Q2 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0001364954/000136495426000085/a9901-financialresultsq220.htm) gives the $120.7M authorisation and the H2 FCF expectation. It is a different document from the same company.

outside_window.finding: Chegg received an NYSE notice under Section 802.01C on 2026-07-24, after its 30-day average close fell below $1.00. The six-month cure runs to about 2027-01-24, and a reverse split is the stated fallback. Shareholders approved reverse-split authority in June 2026, and the board kept the flexibility. A reverse-split announcement could ride with the print, but the deadline and the split itself sit after the window.
Chegg's antitrust suit against Google over AI Overviews is pending, and Google has moved to dismiss. No ruling is dated inside the window.

baseline_tension: There is no skew or usable chain to agree or disagree with. The run-up is flat at -1.8%, so the stock has not repriced the Coursera read or the Skilling deceleration. The mild negative lean cuts against a net cash balance near half the market cap and against a 9.4-day short, which is why p_up sits at 47 rather than lower.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction): the guide-beat finding was cut from +1.0 to +0.5, because the Q2 beat was sold -14.6% on the guide.
Rule 5 (macro-to-company proxy filed small): the Coursera peer read was cut from -1.5 to -1.0, because Chegg and no direct counterparty has confirmed the transmission.
Rule 8 (thin coverage means a bigger move): abs_move_pct was raised from 14 to 15 on a one-analyst name with a new Q4 guide due.
Rule 9 (segment net of the rest): checked. The Skilling finding is already sized small, net of the Academic two-thirds of revenue, so it was left at -1.0.
Rule 7 (positioning): short interest was looked up (DTC 9.4, about 5-6% of shares, not crowded). The negatives stay small and p_up stays at 47.
Rule 4 (financing is a question): the convert repayment is a cash payoff with no dilution, so it is signed positive and small, and a contradicted 'liquidity pressure' claim is rejected.
